title: Download Time Calculator & Bandwidth Speed Estimator
metaDescription: Calculate how long files take to download based on file size and internet connection speed in Mbps and Gbps.
directAnswer: To calculate download time, divide total file size in bits by your internet speed in Megabits per second (Mbps). Because 1 byte equals 8 bits, an internet connection rated at 100 Mbps transfers data at a maximum speed of 12.5 MB/s, meaning a 10 GB file will download in approximately 13.5 minutes.

faq.question: Why doesn't a 100 Mbps internet connection download at 100 MB per second?
faq.answer: Internet speed is measured in Megabits (Mb), while file sizes are measured in Megabytes (MB). Because 8 bits equal 1 byte, a 100 Mbps connection has a peak transfer rate of 12.5 MB/s.

faq.question: How long does a 50 GB game take to download on a 300 Mbps fiber line?
faq.answer: At 300 Mbps (37.5 MB/s), a 50 GB file takes approximately 22 minutes and 45 seconds under ideal network conditions.

faq.question: Does Wi-Fi reduce download speeds compared to an Ethernet cable?
faq.answer: Yes, Wi-Fi introduces radio interference, latency, and packet loss, typically delivering 20% to 50% slower real-world download throughput than direct Ethernet cables.
